description:
FlightData downloads monthly BTS On-Time Performance PREZIP archives. `benchbox/core/flightdata/downloader_specs.yaml` marks 1987-01..1987-09 and 1990-01..1999-12 unavailable (HTTP 404 when probed). Only 327 of 456 months in 1987-2024 can be downloaded. SF10 requests 410 months, so `_months_sequence` silently backfills across the 1990s gap and returns a non-contiguous window of about SF8 (1987-10..2024-12). SF100 in `benchmark_registry.yaml` cannot be reached. Two SF10 cloud bundles (BigQuery 2026-09-20 with 111 synthetic months, Snowflake 2026-09-23 built before the unavailable-month spec) are not publishable.

Research questions:
1. Status of the BTS source: is the 1990s gap permanent, a moved URL, or a different product (for example the TranStats download form, the `Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present` table, or the newer Marketing Carrier dataset)? Re-probe current URLs and document which months exist per source.
2. Alternatives that cover 1987-2024 with the same schema or a mappable one: BTS TranStats form-based download, the ASA Data Expo 2009 airline dataset (1987-2008), Kaggle or Hugging Face mirrors, public cloud datasets (BigQuery public data, AWS Open Data), and archive.org snapshots. Assess licence, provenance, checksum stability, schema parity with `bts_field_names`, and long-term availability for each.
3. Scale-definition options if no complete source exists: cap `scale_options` at the contiguous window (about SF6, 2000-01..2024-12), fail loudly when requested months cannot be supplied, or redefine SF by row count.

Output: a short decision record with a recommended source and scale policy, plus the follow-up implementation item(s). No code changes in this item.
